headline: Jayden Daniels Needed Only 34 Seconds. Washington's No. 5 Is Built for Big Moments
title: Jayden Daniels: 64 Yards in 34 Seconds to Beat Cincinnati
subheadline: With no timeouts left, Daniels moved Washington into range for a walk-off field goal in a 22-20 Monday night win over the Bengals.
description: Jayden Daniels threw for 283 yards, ran for 55 and led a 34-second drive to set up the winning kick as Washington beat Cincinnati 22-20. Why his No. 5 matters.
searchIntent: Commanders fans who watched the Monday night finish want the key facts from the final drive and the right Daniels jersey.
body: Jayden Daniels got the ball at his own 28 with 39 seconds left, no timeouts and Washington trailing Cincinnati 20-19 on Monday night, Nov. 23. Two completions to rookie Antonio Williams, for 22 and 42 yards, put the ball at the Bengals' 8. Drew Stevens then hit a 26-yard field goal as time ran out for a 22-20 win at Northwest Stadium.
Daniels finished with 283 passing yards and led the team with 55 rushing yards.
## Why fans are buying in

This was the second time in 12 days that Daniels won a game in the final minute. On Nov. 12 he threw the go-ahead touchdown with 57 seconds left against the Giants. A quarterback who keeps delivering when the clock is nearly gone is the kind of player a fan base rallies around, and Washington fans have now seen it twice in prime time.

The drive also capped a strong second half. According to the AP, citing OptaSTATS, Washington became the first NFL team in at least 30 years to finish a game with six straight scoring drives of 50 or more yards. The win moved the Commanders to 4-5-1, two games behind the Giants in the NFC East, and snapped Cincinnati's five-game winning streak.

His following has a published number behind it, too. On the NFLPA's year-end Top 50 player sales list, covering licensed player merchandise sold from March 1, 2025 to Feb. 28, 2026, Daniels ranked fifth. That list counts all player products, not jerseys alone.
## The look

The banner above shows his No. 5 in Washington's current styles, including the black alternate. Burgundy and gold remain one of the most recognizable color pairings in the league, and the number is already tied to the franchise's new era.
## Why this jersey will last

In our analysis, Daniels is the player Washington is built around for years to come, and nights like this one are why. The Commanders still have ground to make up in the division, so every late win carries weight from here.

title: Kirill Kaprizov: A Wild-Record 15-Game Point Streak Rolls On
subheadline: Kaprizov had a goal and three assists in a 5-2 win over the Sharks, and the NHL-leading Wild stretched their own point streak to 15 games.
description: Kirill Kaprizov had a goal and three assists in a 5-2 win at San Jose, setting a Wild record with a 15-game point streak. Why his No. 97 is a jersey to own now.

body: Kirill Kaprizov scored once and set up three more goals as Minnesota beat San Jose 5-2 on Monday, Nov. 23. The four-point night gave him a point in 15 straight games, the longest streak in Wild history. He broke his own record of 14 games, set from Nov. 9 to Dec. 9, 2022.
## Why fans are buying in

The streak has been as productive as it has been long. NHL.com counts 32 points for Kaprizov over the 15 games, with eight goals and 24 assists. He now has 19 goals and 49 points in 26 games this season, and Daily Faceoff lists him second in the league in scoring.

The team is matching him. The Wild are 18-3-5, sit first in the NHL standings and have earned a point in 15 straight games themselves, going 12-0-3 since a 5-1 win over Seattle on Oct. 24. When the face of a franchise and the club are both setting the pace, his jersey becomes the obvious one for fans to wear to the rink.

Kaprizov has been Minnesota's signature player since he arrived from Russia, and in our analysis this season is the strongest case yet that he belongs with the league's elite. That is our view, not a sales figure; he does not appear on a published NHL jersey list in our records.

The banner above shows his No. 97 in the Wild's red home jersey and the green alternate. Both lean on the forest-and-wheat palette that sets Minnesota apart from every other team in the league, and the number has been his since his first NHL game.
## Why this jersey will last

A franchise record held by the franchise's best player is the kind of milestone fans remember. Each game the streak continues adds another chapter, and Minnesota's place at the top of the standings gives the season real stakes.

body: Jaden McDaniels scored a career-high 34 points as Minnesota beat Brooklyn 142-116 on Monday, Nov. 23. He made 12 of 16 shots, went 4-for-4 from three and added 10 rebounds and six assists.
It was the third 30-point game of his regular-season career, and the Timberwolves set a season high for points.
## Why fans are buying in

McDaniels built his name in Minnesota as the defender who takes the toughest assignment every night. Nights like this one show a second side of his game. A wing who can guard the other team's best scorer and still put up 34 efficient points is the kind of player fans start to see as a core piece rather than a role player.

He also did it in a team-wide effort. Six Timberwolves scored in double figures, with Ayo Dosunmu adding 23 points, and Minnesota pulled away from a Nets team led by Julius Randle's 29 points in his return to Minnesota.

In our analysis, McDaniels is a jersey for fans who want something beyond the obvious pick. He has spent his whole NBA career in Minnesota, and his growth from a late first-round pick into a two-way starter is a story the fan base has watched up close.
